formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:829-834 — capped when bought > period start (string compare, so a first-day purchase is not capped); a capped row's period return is totalROI = (value − cost) ÷ cost; uncapped rows use periodReturn, which turns 2Y into a yearly rate (:640-643) while capped rows stay totals.
formula_checks.plain_example: VTI: 10 shares at $200 on 15 Jan, 10 at $250 on 15 Jun, $260 now, SPY +10% since 15 Jan. Before: +15.56%, beat SPY by 5.56. Should be: +30.00% time-weighted, beat by 20.00. A purchase on the first day: capped_since blank → should read the first day (label only today).

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:761 — BENCHMARK_TICKER[kind] or SPY; buildPerformance passes p.kind only (:831). The sync writes kind in step with class (src/services/sync/ingest.ts:203-204), but updatePosition (src/store/useStore.ts:808-812) changes the class the person sets and leaves kind as it was.
formula_checks.plain_example: A synced fund the person re-files as a bond keeps kind stocks_etf: before, compared with SPY; should be AGG. A holding nothing describes: before, SPY; should be no yardstick and no beat-by.

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:879-880 — pct = Math.round(share × 100), then the 25% test on the rounded pct; value = Math.round(marketValue). Tie: the first row with the largest value wins (reduce with >).
formula_checks.plain_example: Five holdings, largest $24,600 of $100,000. Before: "VTI is 25% of your investments". Should be: no fact (24.6% is under 25%). Tie order is unsettled but harmless.

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:902-906 — weight = value now ÷ total value of ALL rows (those with no return included); contribution = weight × period return. No screen calls it.
formula_checks.plain_example: VTI $6,000 now (+20%), BND $5,000 (0%). Before: VTI contributes +10.91 points, more than the portfolio's +10%. Should be: +10.00 points (weights $5,000 / $5,000 at the start).

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:939-943 — groups by position.kind (no kind → other_asset), cash above 0 added, each pct rounded to one decimal inside the function. No screen calls it.
formula_checks.plain_example: Three equal $10,000 slices. Before: 33.3% each (sums to 99.9). Should be: 33.333…% each at full precision, rounded once on screen; whether the screen forces the shown three to 100.0 is a display rule no decision states. Grouping by kind has the same class-vs-kind gap as MK-PF-F-013.

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:996-1002 — every date values TODAY's shares × the close on or before it; no price counts as 0; the yardstick line falls back to the value line. No screen calls it.
formula_checks.plain_example: Two holdings with no prices: before, a flat $0 line of 13 points; should be no line. Separately (NEEDS RULING, case UNCLEAR): QQQ bought in June is drawn as held all year — $8,000 at the start where $1,000 was really held.

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:1030-1033 — Σ(return × value NOW) ÷ Σ value now. No screen calls it. MK-NW-F-084 (performance.ts:858-865) already weighs by the start value.
governing_decisions: DEC-0248 (value-weighted — still met by start-value weights)
formula_checks.plain_example: A $2,000 now (+100%), B $1,000 (0%). Before: +66.67%. Should be: $2,000 → $3,000 = +50.00%, the figure MK-NW-F-084 gives for the same holdings.

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:1061-1064 — Σ(yardstick return × value NOW) ÷ Σ value now over rows with a yardstick return (own return not required). Shown on /home as the market figure (src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx:208) and in BENCH (performance.ts:1127).
formula_checks.plain_example: A $2,000 (+100%, its market +10%), B $1,000 (0%, market +2%). Before: "market +7.33%". Should be: +6.00%, weighed by the $1,000 and $1,000 held when the window began.

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: src/domain/performance/index.ts:1091-1092 — 0 for a missing or ≤ −100% return; otherwise Math.round(total × r ÷ (1 + r)). No screen calls it.
formula_checks.plain_example: $100,000 on 9 Sep, $100,000 added 1 Oct, $203,010 today, +2.01% time-weighted. Before: "up $4,000". Should be: up $3,010 (203,010 − 100,000 − 100,000). No return: before $0; should be no figure.

formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: MoneyKeel/functions/networth-and-performance/performance.ts:891 — interest naming no ticker → Cash in this account, whatever account it came from; :898 drops a category that earned 0, its stated bond rate with it. The Performance tab hands it every record in the store (src/screens/PerformanceScreen.tsx:431-436). Money-market point: a fund named or listed as money market is filed Stocks / Funds before asset_class is written (ingest.ts:192-204, DEC-0309), so class cash means cash — the auditor misread that part. Return: start = value ÷ (1 + periodReturn), but a 2Y row's periodReturn is a yearly rate (index.ts:640-643) — not run by a case.
formula_checks.plain_example: Ally CD $25,000 at 4.10% and Marcus CD $15,000 at 3.85% paid $412. Before: "Cash in this account $412", no Bonds & CDs row. Should be: "Bonds & CDs $412, 4.01%/year".
